sections.h2: Who sets and collects tax on a Victoria home
sections.html:
A Victoria bill passes through three offices. Victoria Central Appraisal District puts a value on the property, every taxing unit chooses a rate, and the Victoria County Tax Office mails the statement and collects.

About 66,500 people call Victoria home, a 1.5% rise since 2020. Owners live in 57.9% of homes. The median home is valued at $207,100 and rent runs a median $1,172. Because most homes are modestly priced, a flat school exemption wipes out a big slice of the school value.

Division of labor: the appraisal district sets values, mails appraisal notices, hears protests and runs exemptions. Taxing entities adopt budgets and rates. The assessor-collector figures the bills, collects and passes the money along. Inside city limits, one bill can carry county, school, city and sometimes junior college, hospital or road district charges.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address changes: Victoria Central Appraisal District, 2805 N. Navarro St., Suite 300, phone (361) 576-3621, weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Bills, payments, penalty questions: the Victoria County Tax Office, 205 N. Bridge St., Suite 101, phone (361) 576-3671.
  • City rate and budget questions: the City of Victoria.

Victoria charged $0.4790 per $100 of taxable value in 2025, and its 2026 proposal was $0.4538. Whatever your statement shows controls.

The council's choice falls between two benchmarks: a no-new-revenue rate of $0.4538 and a voter-approval rate of $0.4652 for 2026.

The table covers the city's share only. Ask the tax office for the combined rate on your account.

The county tax office mails statements each October, due on receipt. Lateness starts February 1, which makes January 31 the real deadline.

The penalty starts at 6%, rises one point on the first of each later month, then jumps 2 points on July 1 to hit 12%. Interest is a separate 1% each month. A payment mailed late in January counts only if the post office postmarks the envelope by January 31. A unit that uses a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent on accounts still open in July.

The county tax office receives the certified roll from the appraisal district by July 25, then combines it with each unit's rate to produce the October statements. Appraisal notices go out in mid-April, and rate setting runs from August to September.

  • If no statement arrives by November 1, ask the tax office to mail one. A bill that never arrived does not excuse the tax or release the lien.
  • With an escrow account, put your loan number on any statement that reaches you and forward it to the lender.
  • Lenders have to ask the county for their clients' statements by late August, or the owner may get the bill directly.

You can lower a bill in two ways. File for a homestead on the house you live in, or contest a value that looks too high. Neither happens at the tax office, because the appraisal district takes both.

The general exemption goes to a house that is your main residence on January 1. Owners 65 and up receive an extra exemption, and disabled homeowners, a disabled veteran and a surviving spouse have their own. School districts take $140,000 off a homestead and $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners. A taxing unit may add a percentage exemption too, so ask which local ones apply to the units on your bill.

House Bill 585 sets what an applicant brings:

  • A Texas driver license or ID card copy, where the property address matches the license, a vehicle registration or a utility bill.
  • A signed statement that you claim no other homestead, in Texas or elsewhere.
  • For a manufactured home, a statement of ownership and location from the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs.

Active duty military members and spouses can ask the chief appraiser to waive the address match. You file once, unless the chief appraiser asks you to reapply. Forms are on the district's Forms page, and completed forms go to exemptions@victoriacad.org.

State law also caps homestead value growth at 10% a year after the first qualifying year. Seniors and disabled owners keep a school tax freeze that can follow them to a replacement Texas homestead.

Aim to get the protest notice to the district before May 15. The cutoff is later only when 30 days after your appraisal notice arrives falls past it. The district's taxpayer page has Form 50-132, a guide to filling it out, and a video on presenting a case.

Notices are mailed in mid-April and protests are due May 15. The district takes protests at protest@victoriacad.org. If the review board's order still looks wrong, the next steps are court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

sections.h2: Ways to pay Victoria County property tax
sections.html:
Victoria County accepts payment at a tax office, by mail, by phone or online. You may pay part of the bill, but penalty and interest begin on any balance still open after January 31.

  • At the counter: cash, check, money order, or a debit or credit card with a convenience fee.
  • By phone at 877-253-4085, for Victoria County accounts only. Cards carry a 2.30% fee with a $1 minimum, and an electronic check carries a flat $0.50 fee.
  • By mail: write the account number and the words "partial payment" on a partial payment.
  • A returned check carries a $30 service charge.

Seniors and disabled homeowners can ask about the four-installment option.

sections.h2: Selling a Victoria house with tax owed
sections.html:
On January 1 a lien for the year's tax attaches and stays with the house. For that reason closing agents take the tax out of seller funds. Buyers should read their closing papers, since the title company may have collected from the seller and credited the buyer.

The January 1 owner remains responsible for that year's tax even after selling. Late tax stops title from clearing, so it comes out of the proceeds. Ask the tax office for a balance on every unit before you list.

A buyer who closes mid-year may qualify for the exemption on the rest of that tax year when the seller never held it.

A cash buyer skips lender approval but not the tax payoff. Put the balance figures next to each offer so you can see what you would net. Also ask each buyer who handles repairs and whether the closing date can move if the title company finds an old lien.

faqs.a: In 2025 it was $0.4790 per $100. The 2026 proposal was $0.4538. The tax office, at (361) 576-3671, can confirm the final number.

faqs.q: When does Victoria property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1, though a postmark of January 31 still counts. Penalty (6%) and interest (1%) are then added, and the penalty keeps rising until 12% on July 1.

faqs.q: Which Victoria office changes my value or exemption?
faqs.a: Call Victoria Central Appraisal District, (361) 576-3621. The tax office only bills. Values, exemptions and account details all change at the district.

faqs.q: Can I pay only part of my Victoria tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Mark the check with your account number and the words partial payment. Interest and penalty still build on whatever is unpaid after January 31.

faqs.q: Does a Victoria buyer owe the seller's unpaid tax?
faqs.a: The tax remains attached to the house until cleared. Closing papers show who paid.
